newsitem.title: BULGARIA: THREE BULGARIAN BANKS PLAN TO SERVICE VISA CARDS.
newsitem.headline: THREE BULGARIAN BANKS PLAN TO SERVICE VISA CARDS.

text.p: Three Bulgarian banks are in talks with Visa International's credit card payment system to service its cards locally as the banks that used to provide the service no longer operate, a central bank official said on Friday.

"Bulbank, the United Bulgarian Bank and Post Bank are in talks to service Visa cards. We could licence them (for the service) after they close agreements with Visa," a Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) official who declined to be named told Reuters.

Visa credit card holders cannot use them in Bulgaria since three of the four banks licensed as local Visa operators were ruled insolvent by courts and the fourth had its banking licence waived by the BNB.
"Our bank is ready to start servicing Visa cards as soon as we close negotiations with Visa," Stefan Karagyozov, director of the United Bulgarian Bank (UBB) Banking Cards and Cheque department said.

The UBB, which became Bulgaria's largest private bank after its sale to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, Bulbank and U.S. Oppenheimer & Co. last month, is now authorised as a national operator for Mastercard.
Bulbank, Bulgaria's largest state commercial bank, has been a Visa member since November 1995.
The Bulgarian Post Bank, also a Visa member, expected to complete preparations for operating Visa cards locally within the next two months, Evelina Petkova, an expert at the bank's Card Unit said.
Bankers said depending on negotiations and technical adjustments, Visa card payments in Bulgaria were expected to resume in October at the earliest.
The four banks that used to service Visa card payments were First Private Bank (FPB), the private Trade and Savings Bank (TSBank), state-owned Balkanbank and the Bank for Agricultural Credit (BAC).

In May the BNB retracted FPB's licence after the bank failed to improve its negative capital to risk assets ratio and to resume payments to major creditors. On August 1 the BNB asked the court to open a liquidation procedure for FPB.
The other three banks were ruled insolvent by the Sofia City Court this year.
